preamble: Laxing of the close front rounded vowel [y] to the near-close near-front rounded [ʏ]. In Turkish, /y/ (written ü) is lowered to [ʏ] in the final open syllable of a phrase, as part of a rule that lowers every vowel except /a, o/: köprü [cʰø̞pˈɾʏ] 'bridge', ölü [ø̞ˈl̠ʲʏ] 'dead'. Zimmer & Orgun describe the environment as the final open syllable of a phrase; Göksel & Kerslake, as cited by Wikipedia, describe it as word-final.

languageExamples.context: Final open syllable of a phrase

examples.note: Wikipedia: /i, y, u, e, œ/ are lowered to [ɪ, ʏ, ʊ, ɛ, œ] in this position.
Wiktionary does not apply the rule everywhere: örtü 'cover' is given as [œɾˈty], with unlowered [y].

sources: Zimmer, K., & Orgun, O. (1992). Turkish. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 22(1–2), 43–45. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100300004588
